summary: The bundled runtime is llama.cpp v1.0.0 (b12359, commit b1b770d90d94cad9e9ea5b993bdbc383a522fb28) under runtimes/llama.cpp/b12359 (both archives, LICENSE, runtime.json with the sha256s, the source commit, the Windows add-on zip's sha256 and the help text's sha256); b11669 is removed. The seal's refused list is regenerated from v1.0.0's own --help (new: --allow-unauthenticated-tools, --connect, --connect-code, --media-allow-private-urls, --shard/--ple) and its allow-list admits exactly the new settings. A new module, workbench/runtime_tuning.py, puts v1.0.0's capabilities to work as owner launch defaults (brain.flash_attn, kv_type, load_mode, mtp_draft, batch; each as before by default) plus --jinja --reasoning off always; the memory sum counts the KV type and the MTP head; --cache-ram is sized from the memory sum for every kept prompt (then four). The model check has a time-boxed tuning stage S2T that sweeps flash attention, KV type, batch, threads, offload (Vulkan) and MTP draft length, keeps only settings whose answer is identical to the plain run at temperature 0, reports K13/K14 ('reads/writes at >= 99 tokens a second') and how far off, proposes the best with Undo, and stores the measured rates her clock starts from. Here: the sealed 4B started on v1.0.0 and passed every wall; PLAN's and READ's kept prompts both survived the priming round; the second PLAN turn on Rail Demo took 4,018 ms (K4b: 3,300 ms on b11669, quieter machine). MTP was measured through the sealed path with the 2B MTP GGUF: identical answers, no speed gain on this CPU. Nothing was tested in the owner's sense and nothing ran on the ThinkPad.

Defaults stay as before: flash attention auto (the runtime's own default, as on b11669), KV f16, load mode none (a resident copy), MTP off, batch 64. Each is an owner launch default (Settings, Local model) the model check measures and proposes with Undo. --jinja and --reasoning off are always on (measured here: thinking off without the per-request switch; the per-request switch stays).
A quantized KV cache with flash attention off is refused at configuration (MODEL_KV_TYPE_NEEDS_FLASH_ATTENTION).

The cache sizing: an entry = KV over 1,024 tokens + 6 checkpoints (an upper bound; measured entries carry about 4); 14 kept prompts (11 kinds, PLAN's and READ's desks, the slot's own save), then 4. On the 4B here the 14-rung was admitted (4,669 MiB). On the owner's 35B fixture the estimate becomes 31,930 MiB, under Auto's 32 GiB ceiling; at 37 GiB available it takes the 4-rung (1,588 MiB).
The MTP memory term: the head's KV over the context and 512 MiB for the draft context's buffers (an estimate; the readback checks it).

The tuning stage S2T is in the awake part, boxed at 240 s by default (--tuning-seconds), each row a fresh sealed launch that primes nothing (a new launch option prime=false, only the model check uses it). On the processor it reads 300 and writes 24 tokens a row to fit the box; on Vulkan 1,200 and 64. One dimension at a time from the plain run; a setting is kept only when its answer's sha256 equals the plain run's and her typical question (300 read, 40 written) is faster.

Her clock: the measured rates are kept per model key (config_dir/model-check/measured_rates.json); a key with no timings of its own starts from them (a small read at three fifths), before the 4B stand-ins. The key includes the seal digest, so the rates match only the launch settings they were measured with.

The structured-output path: her kinds' answers stay on her GBNF grammars (stricter than a JSON schema for short lines); the chat plan's JSON answer keeps the server's JSON-schema path as before. Nothing changed there.

release_note: Her model's runtime is llama.cpp v1.0.0 (build b12359), the project's first stable release, in place of b11669. Its newer abilities are yours to switch on, each measured first: flash attention, a half-size prompt memory, loading the model mapped from its file, a larger reading batch, and multi-token prediction with a model file that carries its own MTP head. Her prompt cache is now sized so every question kind she keeps ready stays ready. The model check has a new tuning stage: it tries each setting on your machine, keeps only those that give the same answer, tells you how far reading and writing are from 99 tokens a second, and offers the best under 'Use the measured settings?', with Undo. Her model stays sealed; the seal's lists come from v1.0.0's own help.
